blocks.text: Driven by a nostalgic pushback against sterile and cold mid-century modernism, the architectural revival exploded across American themed restaurants, interior design, and pop culture, diffusing authentic distinct psychedelic-era twists and Gilded Age elements.

The design revival movement became easily recognizable and highly commercialized through a core group of decor elements, such as the abundant indoor ferns hanging plants and potted ferns draped from ceilings to shape conservatory-style, lush, environments, wood, metalwork involving medium-stained exposed brick walls, oak paneling, and gold-plated and heavy brass accents.

Other elements can incorporate multi-colored stained glass lamps (often plastic replicas) Tiffany-style lamps, casting warm, hung low over tables, and patterned light. The "more is more" color palette was often dominated by warm earth tones such as orange, brown, and old gold, balanced out by light lime green and heavy maroon accents, along with Vaudeville typography which can be inscribed with elaborately decorated, bold, slab-serif lettering, utilized heavily in menus, or "old-timey" Tuscan signages. Cultural kitsch from the 1890s, such as trains, penny farthings, and novelty inventions, are also common with the aesthetic.
